title: Schur partition theorem FULL forall-n identity (formalize-only continuation)
flags: known-classical (Schur 1926); formalize-only — do NOT re-fund as novel

OPE-424/OPE-426 partial-ladder disposition: finite certificates n<=24 computable / n<=12 Finset + bridge, zero sorry, Adversarial-approved. FULL forall-n A(n)=B(n) remains OPEN — do not re-prime the closed finite-certificate scope.
target_statement_shape: For all n : ℕ, the number A(n) of partitions of n into distinct parts ≡ 1,2 (mod 3)
equals the number B(n) of partitions of n into parts ≡ ±1 (mod 6):
A(n) = B(n), i.e. card {p : Nat.Partition n // ∀ q ∈ p.parts, q % 3 ∈ [1, 2] ∧ p.parts.Nodup}
= card {p : Nat.Partition n // ∀ q ∈ p.parts, q % 6 ∈ [1, 5]}
recommendation: Second candidate. The generating-function route is the honest path to full forall-n: product expansion prod_{k>=1} (1 + x^(3k+1))(1 + x^(3k+2)) = prod_{m>=6, gcd(m,6)=1} (1 - x^m)^(-1)... but Mathlib v4.10.0 has essentially NO partition-generating-function infrastructure (no PowerSeries usage anywhere under Combinatorics/, no Euler pentagonal, no q-series product identities), so the attack would have to BUILD that infra — that is exactly what makes it valuable to Mathlib but expensive for one sprint. Feasibility shape is NOT finite-checkable: equality for all n needs either a coefficient-extraction identity over PowerSeries or a bijection (Glaisher-style map parts <-> multiplicities mod 3). Recommend scoping the attack as: Level A = Glaisher-style explicit bijection between the two Finset families at fixed n via multiplicity arithmetic (decidable per-n, generalizes by pure algebra on Multiset.count), Level B = lift to the universal statement. Definition risk LOW: STATEMENT pin exists since 2026-08-04 including the swapped-pairing landmine (fails at n=2) — reuse it verbatim, do not restate.
